children: Our Bureau Bengaluru: IT services major Infosys projected a weaker fiscal year outlook as it marginally missed analyst estimates for the second quarter of FY27 reporting a 6.2% year-on-year (YoY) growth in net profit at 7,823 crore. On a quarter on quarter basis profit growth was meagre at 0.7%. At 49,244 crore, revenue grew 10.7% on yearly basis and 2.1% quarter on quarter.

Infosys lowered its guidance for the fiscal year 2027 to 1-2% range in constant currency terms, its weakest estimate in seven years, from an earlier range of 1.5-3%. Last quarter, it had trimmed the upper end from 3.5% earlier. The operating margin was largely falt at 21% in the September quarter. The outlook for operating margin was maintained in the range of 20-22% for the full year.

While the largest region North America degrew alongside manufacturing, retail and hi-tech, growth in Europe, international markets and three sectors including financial services, energy, utilities, resources & services and life sciences supported the September quarter.

Infosys registered a 45% jump in large deal wins and a net addition of 4,500 in employee count. However, the senior management expects even more uncertainty in the macro environment and increasing competitive intensity in projects. "There is AI which is giving us growth, there is AI which is also seeing a compression," said chief executive officer Salil Parekh.

The macro environment, Parekh added, "is also equally in a place where there are continuing different wars. There were some interest rate increases. There was also the 10-year yield, which is now neighbouring to 5%, and there's continuing some element of talent switch, which creates a different type of an environment for the global economy." Further, there will be an offshoring impact of 1% as the US is tightening labour laws pushing software services exporters to hire more locals. "We are looking at higher offshoring through the year," added Parekh, who is set to pass the baton to CEO designate Ashiss Kumar Dash to lead Infosys starting April 2027. After the results, Infosys's US-listed shares - American Depository Receipts - fell over 8% in the pre-market opening.

Before the results, at the Indian markets, Infosys shares closed 0.30% higher at 1154.50 apiece on a slightly weaker BSE index. For the shareholders, Infosys board also proposed an interim dividend of 26 per share, an increase of 13% from last year.

The Bengaluru-headquartered software services firm reported AI revenue at 10.5% of the total, (around $540 million) growing at 29% sequentially. In the previous quarter AI services accounted for 8.2% of the revenue. The AI share is similar to that of its larger rival TCS. ET poll of brokerages estimated YoY profit to grow by 8% to 7,965 crore while revenue to rise by 11% to 49,384 crore.

While Infosys, the last among the top tier IT services companies, lowered both ends of its guidance, its immediate smaller rival HCLTech, which is the only IT major to give out full year guidance, raised the lower end of its outlook estimate with a growth of 2.5-4% (from earlier 1-4%). Its Bengaluru rival Wipro continued to guide weak quarterly outlook with Q3FY27 estimated to be in the negative 1.5% to positive 0.5% range. TCS does not share its outlook.

title: Infosys Q2 Net Profit Rises 6.2%, Projects Weakest Growth in 7 Yrs
